title: Three Years and One Short Lever
subtitle: 未来展望 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 未来展望（宇宙探索·未来与展望）
meta: 主题语境：未来展望（宇宙探索·未来与展望）　|　核心词汇：rocket　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 rocket 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1984 the engineer ① launched the rocket that no worker in the workshop would have counted, and he said the launching was the whole of the year. The ② rocket, meaning the craft itself and not the lever, ran three years and stayed uncounted in the book; a rocket, he said, is the only thing in a workshop that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ rocket in that workshop had the same short lever beside it, and the ④ rocket at the far bench, meaning the part they kept for the children to fit and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A rocket, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the engineer said the counting is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the rocket was the whole of the matter, meaning the ambition and not the craft. The ⑥ rocket, meaning the ambition and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; rocket, he said, is either something you launch or the only word that means both a craft and an ambition. He said the ambition is the part they remember.

By 1989 the ⑦ rocket had become a line in a manual, and the manual had become an argument about the short lever. The ⑧ rocket of the whole thing, the engineer wrote in April, was one workshop and three years of counting; rocket, he said, is either the part at the far bench or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ rocket I remember is the craft counted in the manual, which closed in 1991 and is still counted as the quietest in the workshop. A ⑩ rocket, my mother said in 1993, is the only craft that improves by being counted; every rocket, she said, is an ambition that has agreed to look like a craft. She said the ambition was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 火箭（指车间里每一枚旁边的那一枚）
B. n. 火箭（指那枚火箭本身，与短短的拉杆相对）
C. 固定搭配：launch the rocket 发射这一枚火箭

F. n. 火箭（指说明书里写到、被清点的那一枚）
G. n. 火箭、壮志（指一件事里人人都用却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: launch the rocket 意为“发射这一枚火箭”，1984 年那位工程师把车间里没有一位工人肯清点的一枚火箭做了一遍。
rocket 意为“火箭”，指那枚火箭本身而不是短短的拉杆，它经过了三个年头而在簿子上没有被清点。
rocket 意为“火箭”，指车间里每一枚旁边的那一枚，每一枚旁边都有同一根短短的拉杆。
rocket 意为“火箭”，指最远那张工作台的留给孩子们装的那一件，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
rocket 意为“火箭、壮志”，指一件事里人人都用却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这枚壮志就是那件事的全部。
rocket 意为“壮志”，指人人都用却无人提起的那样东西而不是那枚火箭，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
rocket 意为“火箭”，指说明书里写到、被清点的那一枚，到 1989 年这一枚成了说明书里的一行。
rocket 意为“火箭之事”，工程师四月写道，整件事的火箭之事是一处车间和三个年头的清点。
rocket 意为“火箭”，我记得的是说明书里清点过的那一枚，1991 年装好了，至今仍被说成车间里最安静的一枚。
rocket 为抽象总称，母亲 1993 年说，火箭是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的火箭。
